purpose: This tool turns probability into something you can build and count. You list every outcome, pick the ones in an event, and write a fraction. Then you see how probability can come from areas and always stays between 0 and 1.

stops.title: Tap to build
stops.text: You work by tapping. In mode 1, tap a picture in the top row to add it to My sample space, and tap it in your list to remove it. In mode 2 and 4, tap outcomes to turn them yellow. In mode 3 build questions, drag the two round handles.
stops.try: Tap the six dice faces, then press Check my list.

stops.title: Four modes
stops.text: These four buttons switch the activity: 1 list the outcomes, 2 pick an event, 3 find chance by area, 4 chance limits. The Next steps switch them for you. You can also press them yourself.
stops.try: Press 2 Events, then come back to 1 Sample space.

stops.title: Experiment or Question
stops.text: In mode 1 this menu picks the experiment: a coin, a die, two coins, a marble bag or two dice. In the other modes it is called Question and picks the problem. Two coins and two dice need care, because order matters.
stops.try: Pick Flip two coins and list all four outcomes.

stops.title: Write the fraction
stops.text: Choose the top number (outcomes in the event) and the bottom number (all outcomes). They show up in mode 3 read questions, and in modes 2 and 4 after your tapped event is right. A bar shows 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).
stops.try: In mode 3, count the green squares and pick your top and bottom numbers.

stops.title: Check your answer
stops.text: Check tells you if your list, event or fraction is right and explains any mistake. In build questions it is called Check my board. Clear starts over. A wrong answer costs nothing.
stops.try: Press Check before you finish and read the hint.

stops.title: What Next does
stops.text: Step 1 lists a die's outcomes. Step 2 picks an event, such as an even number. Step 3 uses a dart board, where regions are not equal. Step 4 shows an impossible event (0) and a certain one (1).

stops.title: Quick check
stops.text: Two questions at the end. A wrong answer explains why.

teacher: Project mode 1 with two dice and ask: how many outcomes, 11 or 36? Typical mistake: counting totals instead of equally likely pairs, and saying a dart is 1/3 likely to hit each of 3 regions. In the area mode, ask students to build a board where red is 1/4.
